Recurrent Neural Networks are a type of neural network that specializes in processing sequences. A common application of RNNs is for Natural Language Processing due to its effectiveness at handling long and unstructured text. The motivation behind this work came from the observation that, while we have many datasets with information about each word's position within the sequence (such as parts-of-speech), there are very few such datasets where the words themselves can be labeled. This motivates our focus on learning both labels as well as positions over time, building into an end-to-end system which allows us not only to learn the best possible feature extractor but also obtain useful insights into how data about different entities interact together throughout the conversation. Our contributions include: We introduce Conversation-RNN: An architecture specifically designed to model interactions between multiple discourse participants using Recurrent Neural Networks; On diverse domains: Our approach is able to generalize across three domains - (1) restaurant reviews, (2) news articles, and (3) social media posts. In all cases, it outperforms strong baselines; Insightful results: We show in detail what features contribute most strongly towards the task of determining the next sentence label; Prediction accuracy versus training time: We demonstrate experimentally that predictions made by Conversation-RNN converge faster than those obtained via other models when trained under identical conditions. The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 summarizes related works, including some recent advances. Sections 3 gives details regarding our proposed model, along with experimental results showing advantages compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Finally, conclusions are given in section 4. Related Work Researchers have addressed similar problems like ours before, albeit without recurrent connections. For example, (Nguyen et al., 2005) discuss several methods for predicting mutual attention scores between two sentences based upon their syntactic similarity. (Wang Jiang, 2010) propose elements for developing a transition-based dependency parser based on synchronous context-free grammars. However, these previous methods do not address aspects such as entity identification or explicit modeling of temporal relationships between events. Also unlike these earlier efforts, the current research does not require any hand-crafted linguistic rules or edit distance measures. As discussed below however, existing techniques may provide guidance toward better performing systems. Modeling Temporal Information While early attempts used linear chains (i.e., Markov Models) (Church Hanks, 1990), more complex non-linear models were later developed for various applications. For example, Hidden Markov Model (HMM) was successfully applied in speech recognition (Rabiner, 1989). Recently, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) (Elman, 1990; Hochreiter Schmidhuber, 1997) have been widely adopted for sequence modeling because they capture long-term dependencies among inputs through hidden states. Inspired by these developments, researchers began applying them to natural language generation tasks like machine translation (Bojar et al., 2006). In contrast to such traditional uses of RNNs, which seek to generate one single output per input, the main goal of Sequence-to-Sequence Learning (SSTL) tasks is usually to extract sequential patterns rather than produce outputs directly. One popular example is presented by (Bahdanau et al., 2014a). Here authors use SSTL networks to predict human-level sentiment for English tweets. They then extend this technique to Chinese tweets using an adaptation layer (Gong, 2015). Following closely after the success of CNNs on ImageNet classification task (Krizhevsky et al., 2012), another major breakthrough in deep architectures has come recently thanks to LeCun et al.. These authors showed that convolutional layers help deal with low level visual perception tasks beyond finding edges such as object detection, segmentation, etc. By transferring knowledge learned in images to transcripts gathered from chatbots, they also revealed potential improvements to automatic evaluation metrics for spoken dialogue systems. Convolution filters operating on image signals often correspond to convolutions performed on continuous-time signals called LSTMs. Therefore, inspired by the use of dilated convolution operations (Heinrich et al., 2016), Grave et al. incorporated dilations inside the structure of their Long Short-Term Memory network (GSD-LSTM). In doing so, they achieved significantly improved performance over standard LSTMs on several benchmark tasks, (Graves et al., 2017a). More precisely, GSD-LSTM achieves a significant improvement in relation extraction since they leverage key frames extracted from the video instead of simply extracting neighboring pixels during decoding times. Further, they tackle the problem of missing tokens in real-life scenarios, e.g., in case of dialogues recorded by the microphone arrays surrounding speakers. Such situations result in discontinuous datasets meaning that labels cannot be assigned too far away from the initial ones (Etzioni et al., 2004). I had planned on joining my sister and nephew at Lake Isabel for some boating fun. Dad called me from the beach not long after 10am saying he needed to go back home immediately. The diner was a warm oasis in the cold, shitty expanse of the nighttime cityscape. Night owl patrons slurp burnt coffee and chew on lukewarm food. A gruff, overweight line cook is mopping up grease with tongs. Next to them sits an enigmatic-looking man reading a newspaper. No one else at the diners seems interested in what he's thinking or who he knows. His posture is stoical and his expression rigidly neutral. He has no interest in talking about himself - he just wants to read some news from somewhere far away. As if by magic, the magazine magically disappears as soon as it touches him. The story starts again right where it left off without any interruptions from anyone outside that room. If you were close enough you'd be able to feel the electricity coursing through the bones of your body when he gets excited for something - and then it's gone exactly like lightning once he realizes he can't act on the impulse because there are too many things to do before dawn. He doesn't have a specific reason why people don't want to talk to him; they ignore him whenever he approaches them. But the truth is they all know this person well. Even though he never speaks directly to anyone except those closest to him, everyone keeps knowing everything about him. Then comes another weekday morning. It's almost noon now but there will still be no customers until after 3 p.m. On these days nobody even waits in line anymore; everybody rushes in early hoping not to miss anything important.

I could pinpoint the one moment the sky came crashing down on me. Things had been going so well, work at the office had been steady and fun as normal, I was having a good time with my friends and closest family over Thanksgiving. It all went to shit in one minute. It started out pretty innocently; I got into an argument with someone about something they said or did that made me angry, which immediately turned it into an emotional fight between two people who didn't even know each other. My senior manager asked if we should have stood firm and just left but he insisted we ended up fighting some back and she ended up hurting myself badly enough to end my day early. That's when everything changed for me. The next morning after getting home from work; I decided not to pay attention to her anymore because no matter what I do I can't force anyone else to like me. But sometimes things happen outside of your control and that's where we start screaming "why?" The first few days were rough; I felt depressed almost constantly. She told me that part of her problem is she doesn't want to be hurt by another person. There isn't much more to say except to hate yourself for thinking such thoughts but I'm not sure there is any way around them completely because everyone has different levels of tolerance. We talked about guilt and forgiveness but nothing seemed able to rectify it; instead it only added fuel to the fire. None of us deserve to feel unsafe every single day. Lastly, I am thankful that things worked out for the best even though I hate feeling guilty adding insult to injury while still learning new ways to protect myself. Maybe someday I'll be able to forgive myself entirely but right now it's better to learn from experiences rather than letting feelings cloud my judgment.

Jensen loved fishing with his dad. Since he was only five, his dad only let him use a kid's fishing pole. After much pleading, his dad finally let him use the whole rod. In addition to being an avid fisherman, Jensen also enjoys shooting airsoft guns in real life and playing soccer in virtual worlds. Early career Since childhood, Jensen has wanted to be a singer or actor; however, when asked by friends about what else they could do besides singing, he replied that he would like to play guitar since it is one of his favorite instruments, which lead others to suggest becoming a musician instead. His interest in photography began at age 14, after being inspired by his cousin who had taken pictures for all kinds of events (including weddings). At age seventeen, though without any formal training on how to take photos, Jensen began doing some work for local talent agencies. He even took part in auditions during high school but didn't get selected as many times as he expected. In 2009, after graduating from middle school, Jensen enrolled in Gakushuin University where he majored in Fine Arts. Solo projects When accepting university admission, Jensen planned to pursue his dream of being an independent artist. However, due to financial pressure in Japan, he decided to volunteer as an intern for Sony PlayStation Co., Ltd. (Sony's subsidiary) - a Japanese electronics company - and subsequently applied there as well. On July 10, 2010, Sony announced through its official website that Jensen would become their first international employee under Overseas Expansion Team. While working for Sony, he participated in various tasks including preparing presentations, leading seminars concerning internal business support systems, creating marketing materials such as posters and brochures, helping manage employees' social media profiles, translating emails between English and Japanese, among other things. The experience gained while working for Sony helped shape his future plans. His first solo project entitled Taste of Coffee debuted January 24, 2012. It includes songs called "Coffee," "Maple," "Honey," "Strawberry Smoothie" (English lyrics), "Waffle Fries" (Japanese translation), "Ramen Noodle," "Milk," "Papaya Lychee," "Doughnuts," "Buns," "Almond Melon," "Green Tea" (both songs are original compositions composed by Sandy Chen). Later in February, another six additional tracks were released: "Lemon Barrel," "Ice Cream Bite," "Jelly" (also composed by Sandy Chen), "Toy Store," "Firefly Cosmic Light Projection," and "Pumpkin Spice Latte." On June 3, 2013, Jensen signed a contract with Universal Music Group Japan. Two days later, Madison Avenue Records through its YouTube channel released the cover artworks, video teaser clips, background story, and two songs: "Kana Kana" and "Upside Down World"; "Tea Bag Chocolate" would be released September 11 that same year. Less than three months later, the album's title was revealed to be: I Love You Madly. Alongside the release, both digitally downloaded versions and physical CD versions of Upside Down World became available across digital retailers around the globe. Personal life As of March 2015, Jensen resides in New York City.
